messages:
matt: Quick proposal — moving to explicit lease-epoching for credits attribution and audit windows. Instead of trying to derive a single global watermark, each ingest shard would publish a lease_epoch id that maps to a bounded accounting window. This keeps late-arrival handling local to the shard and makes audits deterministic.

asha: Hmm — can you sketch how a lease_epoch differs from our current handshake + watermark?

matt: Sure. Today we have a handshake that assigns a claim id + a fluid watermark. With lease_epoch, the flow is: shard picks epoch ID (monotonic), tags every event with epoch, and emits epoch-finalization events when it reaches checkpoint. The reconciler treats epoch as a stable boundary so compaction and audits reference epoch ids instead of timestamps.

jordan: Sounds like it would simplify compaction logic. Where do we handle long-tail late credits (weeks-months)? Do epochs prevent backfill?

matt: They don't prevent backfill. Backfills are still append-only events targeted at a specific epoch. But since epoch ids are stable boundaries, reconciliation can apply backfills deterministically to the impacted epoch(s) and emit an audit delta.

lee: What about cross-shard attribution when a single request fans out? Attribution currently relies on a root claim id propagated across services. Would we keep root ids plus epoch tags?

matt: Yes — root claim ids continue to exist for lineage. Epoch is orthogonal: it scopes the accounting window the event will be counted in. So a fanout message will carry both a root_claim and epoch_id.

asha: Are we introducing a new API surface (clients need to set epoch) or will epochs be assigned by ingress?

jordan: We should keep ingress assigning epochs to avoid client complexity. Clients just send requests; the gateway/sidecar stamps epoch.

matt: Agreed — ingress stamps. Client-visible only in audit reports and when customers query ledger slices.

lee: How does this interact with SLA handoffs and Dedicated vs Hosted? Dedicated fleets might prefer longer epoch durations for throughput efficiency, hosted shorter for near-realtime billing. Do we support configurable epoch windows per deployment?

matt: Yes — epoch duration is a policy on the ingress pool. Policy picks: epoch_duration_ms and finalization_rules (e.g., idle + max-duration). That way Dedicated could pick 10m epochs, hosted 1m.

infra-bot: CI: metering/epoching PR ran e2e on staging: 1 failed test (compaction-finalizer). See link: https://ci.example/1234

asha: Two concerns: (1) audits need human-friendly identifiers — epoch_2026-04-01-23 rather than opaque 64-bit ints, (2) replays: if we replay an epoch stream for backfill, we need deterministic ordering. Are we hashing ordering keys?

matt: Good points. Plan: epoch ids are human-encoded (region-pool-YYYYMMDDThhmm). Ordering inside epoch by (ingest_seq, event_offset). We already have ingest_seq per shard. Replayer uses that for deterministic application.

jordan: Edge case: what if a shard loses state and reassigns an epoch id that overlaps previously finalized epoch due to clock drift? We need a lease TTL + coordinator-enforced monotonic allocation.

matt: Exactly — lease_epoch allocator is coordinated (etcd/consul) and will reject re-use of a finalized epoch id. The allocator issues ephemeral leases; finalization moves epoch to an immutable list.

lee: Sounds promising. Next steps? RFC or PR?

matt: I'll write a short RFC with the API sketches and compaction/finalizer delta handling. Will include example audit queries and backfill flow. Ping me if you want to be reviewer. :thumbsup:

asha: I'll review — please include a failure-mode section (coordinator partition, long replays).

jordan: Add performance numbers for epoch durations vs batching savings. I can run a quick sim.

matt: Thanks all — filing RFC today.
